intro: Lesson 29: Riba and why Islam forbids it. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.h: Case study: Bilal wants a car

panels.title: Option 1: a car loan
panels.text: The bank lends Bilal £10,000. He must pay back £11,500 over three years: the extra £1,500 is interest on the loan.

panels.title: Option 2: murabahah
panels.text: A provider buys the car for £10,000 and sells it to Bilal for £11,500, a known price agreed at the start, paid in instalments. The provider owns the car before selling it.

questions.q: Which option is permitted, and why?
questions.a: Murabahah: it is a sale at a known profit, and Allah has permitted trade (2:275). The car loan is riba: an increase on a loan.

questions.q: Explain how a musharakah could work for a family shop.
questions.a: Partners put in money together and share the profit and the loss in agreed proportions.

passage.title: al-Baqarah 2:275
paras: Allah has permitted trade and has forbidden riba.

panels.title: How serious is it?
points: Allah declares war on those who keep riba (2:279)
The Prophet ﷺ cursed its taker, giver, writer and witnesses
One of the seven destructive sins

panels.title: Harms of riba
points: The lender gains with no risk

head: Musharakah
Murabahah
rows: Sells at a known, fixed profit

a goodly loan with no increase
cost-plus sale: selling at a known profit

questions.q: Explain two reasons Islam forbids riba. (4 marks, our own question)
questions.a: It is injustice: the lender gains without risk while debt grows on the borrower; Allah forbids it clearly (2:275) and the Prophet ﷺ cursed all involved (Muslim).

questions.q: A loan with no increase is called ...

questions.a: Interest loan is riba (2:275); murabahah is a sale at a known profit; musharakah shares profit and loss in the shop
